newsitem.title: UK: GKN extends gains after meeting, upgrades.
newsitem.headline: GKN extends gains after meeting, upgrades.

text.p: Shares in British engineering group GKN Plc extended sharp gains on Wednesday after an upbeat analysts meeting and earnings upgrades followed the group's better-than-expected interim results.
The shares were up 68p to 11.54 stg by 1055 GMT after easing from a peak of 11.62, the highest level seen since October last year.
Analysts expected current year forecasts around the 385 million stg level would be raised to the 400 million stg level.
Market sources said Merrill Lynch was among those planning to raise estimates and Credit Lyonnais Laing upped current year forecasts by 20 million stg.
"The meeting was very positive," said Daniel Bevan at Credit Lyonnais Laing. "The highlights being margin improvements in automotives and defence."
Bevan said GKN remained one of his key "buys" of the year and gave a near-term share price target of 12.00 stg.
"The company also said the currency effects will be less in the second half," Bevan said.
GKN earlier announced first half pre-tax profits of 203 million stg, up 12.2 percent on the previous year and above the consensus forecast.
The company said the negative impact of the strong pound on profits was 18 million stg, above the 10 million originally anticipated.

Dealers said the stock was also being lifted by the relative weakness of the pound against the German mark. Sterling slid under the DM3.02 level as investors began to think that UK interest rates might be left unchanged after this week's monetary meeting, traders said.
